title: Finite-type ideals and universal exactness for flat closed subfamilies
statement:
Let $T$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $X\to T$ and $Z\to T$ be finitely presented morphisms (locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], quasi-compact and quasi-separated), and let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed immersion over $T$ [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Assume $Z\to T$ is flat [def-weil-flat-morphism]. Define $\mathcal I=\ker(\mathcal O_X\to i_*\mathcal O_Z)$, where $(i_*\mathcal O_Z)(U)=\mathcal O_Z(i^{-1}U)$. Then $i$ is finitely presented and $\mathcal I$ is a quasi-coherent module of finite type [pqf-def-coherent]. For every $g:T'\to T$, write $X'=X\times_TT'$, $Z'=Z\times_TT'$, $g_X:X'\to X$, and $i':Z'\hookrightarrow X'$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Ordinary module pullback [def-pc-module-pullback] carries the ideal sequence to a short exact sequence
$$0\longrightarrow g_X^*\mathcal I\longrightarrow\mathcal O_{X'}\longrightarrow i'_*\mathcal O_{Z'}\longrightarrow0.$$
In particular the canonical map $g_X^*\mathcal I\to\ker(\mathcal O_{X'}\to i'_*\mathcal O_{Z'})$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 02FV (lemma-finite-presentation-permanence), (2); Tag 01TV (lemma-closed-immersion-finite-presentation). Universal exactness is the affine-local application of algebra.tex Tag 00HL (lemma-flat-tor-zero) to the flat quotient over the base.

proof.text: For affine $V=\operatorname{Spec}R\subseteq T$ and $U=\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq X$ mapping into $V$, the closed immersion gives $i^{-1}U=\operatorname{Spec}(A/J)$. The affine finite-presentation criterion for $X/T$ and $Z/T$ makes $A$ and $B=A/J$ finitely presented over $R$. Discarding the relations in a presentation makes $A$ finite type over $R$; the intermediate-algebra lemma makes $B$ finitely presented over $A$. For each $z\in Z$, choose $V$ around its image and $U$ around $i(z)$ inside the inverse image of $V$; then $i^{-1}U$ is the required affine neighbourhood of $z$. Thus $i$ is locally of finite presentation. A closed immersion is affine; affine permanence gives quasi-compactness and separatedness, hence quasi-separatedness. Thus $i$ is finitely presented.

source.place: Tag 02FV, lemma-finite-presentation-permanence (1), proof via Algebra Tag 00F4, lemma-compose-finite-type (4); Tag 01TQ, lemma-locally-finite-presentation-characterize

proof.text: On an arbitrary affine $U=\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq X$, the ideal description gives $\mathcal I|_U=\widetilde J$ and $i^{-1}U=\operatorname{Spec}(A/J)$; in particular $\mathcal I$ is quasi-coherent. Local finite presentation of $i$ and the affine criterion make $A/J$ finitely presented over $A$. The presentation-kernel lemma with zero variables, applied to $A[\ ]=A\twoheadrightarrow A/J$, makes $J$ finitely generated. Clause (a) of the quasi-coherent finite-type affine criterion makes $\mathcal I|_U$ of finite type. This on an affine covering proves that $\mathcal I$ is of finite type.

source.place: Tag 01TV, lemma-closed-immersion-finite-presentation, proof; Algebra Tag 00R2, lemma-finite-presentation-independent with n=0

proof.text: Fix any $g:T'\to T$. The affine-diagram lemma supplies $i'$, the canonical maps $a,b$, their three quasi-coherent terms, the pushforward comparison and an affine covering $Q=\operatorname{Spec}(A\otimes_RR')$. Its section identifications carry $a,b$ to $J\otimes_RR'\to A\otimes_RR'\to B\otimes_RR'$, with precisely the inclusion and quotient maps, not merely abstract isomorphic terms. On each such chart $B$ is flat over $R$ by the affine flatness criterion for $Z\to T$. The sequence $0\to J\to A\to B\to0$ is short exact since $B=A/J$, also as $R$-modules since scalar restriction changes neither kernels nor surjectivity. Apply the relative-flat tensor-chart criterion with $Y=X'$, chart rings $(R,A,S)=(R,A,R')$ and modules $(L,M,N)=(J,A,B)$; the affine-diagram formulas give its two commuting squares: the sheaf sequence of $a,b$ is short exact and its canonical factorization onto $\ker b$ is an isomorphism. The affine-diagram comparison identifies this sequence with ordinary pullback of the original ideal sequence, as required.
